review:
[BLOCKING] `orders/service.py`, `pick_up` (lines 103–109): the pickup time is never saved.
- `store.get` returns a deep copy. The store docstring says changing a copy changes nothing until it is written back.
- `pick_up` sets `order.picked_up_at` on that copy, logs "picked up", and returns the copy. It never calls `store.save` or any other store method.
- Any call on an order in `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` therefore succeeds, and the caller sees `picked_up_at` set on the returned object. The stored order still has `picked_up_at = None`.
- Later reads, ETA tracking, and the `picked_up_at is not None` duplicate guard all see no pickup. The guard never fires, so a repeated call "succeeds" again with a new timestamp that is also lost.
- Fixing this with a plain `store.save(order)` would overwrite concurrent changes such as a status change or a cancel. It would also stamp the time without a compare-and-set. The write should go through a store method that checks the status and sets `picked_up_at` under the lock, like `update_status`.

[NIT] `orders/service.py`, line 107: `now or datetime.now(...)` accepts a naive `now` without complaint. A naive datetime would be stored next to the timezone-aware UTC values used elsewhere. Consider rejecting a `now` that has no tzinfo.
